description: termination_notice_band (D-68): the BCEA default and the domestic sector's SD7 override, carried over unchanged from termination_rule_set's retired notice_weeks_* columns; and SD1's own two-band notice regime, clause 23(1), read for the first time here. NOT verified.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997, ss 37 and 41
termination_notice_band.notes: Carried over from termination_rule_set.notice_weeks_* (D-68) — the same figure, the same citation, now with its own unit instead of an implied week. service_from/service_to touch the adjacent band exactly, in the same unit both sides, by construction — the reconciliation check in statutory/checks.py relies on that rather than converting between units.

SD7's 6-months-and-over and over-1-year columns held the same figure (4 weeks), so this is one open-ended band rather than a redundant third one with no real boundary.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Sectoral Determination 1: Contract Cleaning Sector, current consolidated text (clauses 3, 8-24), clause 23(1)(a)
termination_notice_band.notes: 'during the first four weeks of employment, not less than one working day's [notice]'. A DAY, not a fraction of a week — see the model docstring. service_from/service_to touch the adjacent band exactly, in the same unit both sides, by construction — the reconciliation check in statutory/checks.py relies on that rather than converting between units.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Sectoral Determination 1: Contract Cleaning Sector, current consolidated text (clauses 3, 8-24), clause 23(1)(b)
termination_notice_band.notes: 'four weeks, if the employee has been employed for more than four weeks'. D-158: exactly four weeks resolves HERE, not to band 1 — see the module docstring for why that is not the most literal reading of clause (b) alone.
